description.narrative: In early August Chad experienced unprecedented torrential rains causing significant damage in several parts of the capital, N’Djamena. These rains persisted until late September and floods expanded to many provinces, causing catastrophic levels of human and material damage, and loss of livelihoods for a significant portion of the population. Red Cross of Chad (RCC) assisted populations in N´Djamena after the initial floods, but assessments carried out in 17 provinces by the National Society (NS) teams between 5 August and 25 September, which found a total of 747,588 people (125,269 households) were affected by the flooding. Through this Emergency Appeal, the IFRC and its members are seeking CHF 5 million to support RRC in the response to this flooding. The strategy of the IFRC response will be to contribute to meet the urgent needs of 239,054 people in 7 provinces and will focus on the following areas, Integrated Assistance, WASH, and Protection and Prevention. IFRC Secretariat funding requirements: CHF 3 million Federation-wide funding requirements: CHF 5 million DREF Allocation: CHF 405,525

This is a contribution to IFRC's Emergency Appeal for Flooding in Chad. It is composed of 100k from the Disaster Fund and 50k Gfunds. Due to delays at IFRC, we do not yet have the PMN number but have been given permission to exceptionally proceed without it.
